heroIntro: For overseas Bangladeshi parents, grandparents, and siblings residing across the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, or Australia, transferring real estate assets, residential flats, or ancestral land in Bangladesh to children or close relatives is most strategically executed through a **Heba Deed (হেবা দলিল - Gift Deed under Muslim Personal Law)**. Unlike general commercial sale deeds (সাফ কবলা দলিল) which attract heavy ad-valorem stamp duties, municipal transfer taxes, and advance source taxes totaling 8% to 15% of property valuation, a Heba executed among designated blood relations enjoys extraordinary statutory tax exemptions, requiring only a nominal fixed stamp duty of BDT 100. However, executing a Heba from abroad demands strict compliance with Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908, the Transfer of Property Act 1882, and consular authentication protocols. An improperly drafted gift deed can trigger costly civil challenges by excluded relatives or be rejected by the Sub-Registrar. This master legal guide explores the theological and legal essentials of Heba, the 33 eligible blood relations, the vital distinction with Heba-bil-Ewaz, embassy execution steps, and post-registration e-Namjari mutation.

quickAnswer.heading: Heba Deed from Abroad: Essential Legal Rules
points: Mandatory written registration: Under Section 17(1) of the Registration Act 1908, an oral Heba is void; every gift of immovable property must be executed via a registered deed.
Three legal essentials: Declaration of gift (Ijab) by donor, Acceptance (Qubul) by donee, and Delivery of possession (actual or constructive).
Fixed BDT 100 Stamp Duty applies ONLY among 33 statutory degrees of blood relationships (husband-wife, parents-children, siblings, grandparents-grandchildren).
Gifting to distant relatives (cousins, in-laws) does NOT qualify for the BDT 100 exemption and attracts general gift taxes.
Overseas donors can execute a Consular Special Power of Attorney abroad authorizing a trusted agent to sign and register the Heba deed before the Sub-Registrar.
Irrevocability: A registered Heba between close blood relations becomes 100% irrevocable once registered and possession is delivered; the donor cannot unilaterally cancel it.
Complete the transfer: Apply online for e-Namjari mutation at mutation.land.gov.bd within 28 days of deed issuance to update government land revenue records.

sections.h2: 1. The Juridical Concept of Heba Under Muslim Personal Law
sections.content:
Under classical Islamic jurisprudence and Bangladeshi civil law, Heba (হেবা) is defined as an immediate, unconditional transfer of property made voluntarily and without consideration (বিনা পণে) by one living person (donor / ওয়াহিব) to another (donee / মৌহুব লাহু) and accepted by or on behalf of the latter.

Unlike a Will (ওয়াসিয়ত / Wasiyat), which only takes effect upon the testator's death and is strictly capped at one-third (1/3rd) of the estate unless other legal heirs consent, a Heba takes effect immediately during the lifetime of the donor. A Muslim landowner of sound mind and legal majority has the absolute, unfettered legal right to gift the entirety (100%) of their self-acquired or ancestral property to any person, even if such gift completely disinherits other natural heirs.

sections.h2: 2. The Three Inviolable Legal Essentials of a Valid Heba
sections.content:
Under established Supreme Court jurisprudence (reiterated in 54 DLR 281 and 19 BLC 412), a valid Heba requires three concurrent theological and legal essentials:

  1. Declaration of Gift (ইজাব / Ijab): An explicit, unambiguous statement by the donor manifesting an immediate intention to divest themselves of ownership and vest title in the donee without coercion or undue influence.
  2. Acceptance of Gift (কবুল / Qubul): Express or implied acceptance by the donee. If the donee is a minor child, acceptance must be made on their behalf by the legal guardian (father, paternal grandfather, or court-appointed guardian).
  3. Delivery of Possession (দখল অর্পণ): The donor must completely divest themselves of dominion and control, handing over actual physical possession or constructive possession to the donee.

sections.h2: 3. Mandatory Registration Requirement: Section 17 Registration Act 1908
sections.content:
Historically, oral gifts under Islamic law were recognized in Bengal without written documentation. However, widespread fraud and forged inheritance claims prompted a comprehensive legislative overhaul in 2004:

Section 17(1)(aa) of the Registration Act, 1908: Substituted by the Law Reforms Ordinance 2004, it mandates that every instrument of gift of immovable property under Muslim law (Heba) MUST be compulsorily registered. An unregistered or oral Heba has zero legal validity in Bangladesh, cannot be relied upon in civil courts, and cannot be used to mutate names in government land revenue records.

sections.h2: 4. The 33 Designated Blood Relations for Fixed BDT 100 Stamp Duty
sections.content:
To encourage family asset consolidation, the government of Bangladesh provides extraordinary fiscal concessions under the Stamp Act 1899 and Finance Act for gifts made among 33 specific degrees of blood relationships:

  • Husband to Wife and Wife to Husband (স্বামী ও স্ত্রী)
  • Father / Mother to Son / Daughter (পিতা-মাতা ও সন্তান)
  • Grandfather / Grandmother to Grandson / Granddaughter (দাদা-দাদী, নানা-নানী ও নাতি-নাতনী)
  • Full Brothers and Sisters (সহোদর ভাই ও বোন)
  • Brother's son/daughter to Paternal Uncle/Aunt (and reciprocal relations defined under statutory rules)

If the gift is made within these 33 degrees, the ad-valorem stamp duty (which is otherwise 1.5% to 3%) is slashed to a nominal fixed fee of just BDT 100.

sections.h2: 6. Step-by-Step Procedure to Execute a Heba Deed from USA, UK & Canada
sections.content:
When the expatriate donor or donee resides overseas, follow this exact legal roadmap:

  1. Drafting the Heba Declaration & Special Power of Attorney: Your advocate in Dhaka drafts a Special Power of Attorney for Heba Registration under Form 1 of the 2015 Rules, accompanied by the draft Heba Deed specifying the property schedule and relation.
  2. Consular Attestation Abroad: The donor attends the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission in Washington DC, New York, London, Ottawa, etc., signing the deed before the Consular Officer with photographs affixed.
  3. MOFA & DC Office Endorsement in Dhaka: The original document is couriered to Dhaka, authenticated at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Segunbagicha, and stamped at the Deputy Commissioner's office under Section 18 of the Stamp Act.
  4. Execution at Sub-Registry: The nominated attorney attends the Sub-Registry Office with the donee (or donee's representative). The Sub-Registrar verifies the relationship through birth certificates/NID, collects the nominal BDT 100 fee, and registers the Heba Deed.
  5. Obtaining the Registered Deed: The Sub-Registrar issues an official Receipt (রসিদ / Form 52). The certified copy (নকল) is typically ready within 7 to 15 days.

sections.h2: 7. Statutory Government Fees, Taxes & Stamp Duty Breakdown (2026)
sections.content:
For an eligible Heba deed among the 33 designated blood relations, the exact statutory government fee breakdown at the Sub-Registry is remarkably minimal:

  • Stamp Duty (স্ট্যাম্প শুল্ক): Fixed at BDT 100 (paid via Non-Judicial Stamp or Treasury Chalan).
  • Registration Fee (নিবন্ধন ফি): Fixed at BDT 100 under Article A(1) of the Registration Table of Fees.
  • Local Government Tax: Exempted (BDT 0).
  • Advance Source Tax (AIT Section 125): Exempted (BDT 0).
  • E-Fee (নকলনবিশের পারিশ্রমিক): BDT 200–300 depending on page count.
  • N-Fee (কপি বালামের ফি): BDT 240.
  • Total Government Cost: Approximately BDT 2,500 to BDT 5,000, regardless of whether the flat is worth BDT 50 Lakh or BDT 10 Crore!

sections.h2: 8. Constructive Delivery of Possession for Overseas Donors & Donees
sections.content:
Because both donor and donee may reside thousands of miles away in New York or London, physical handover of the key or soil is impossible. Under Bangladeshi law, Constructive Delivery of Possession (অনুমানমূলক বা প্রতীকী দখল অর্পণ) is 100% legally recognized:

  • Handing over the original registered title deeds (মূল দলিল) and historical Khatians to the donee.
  • Instructing tenants or commercial caretakers in writing to pay all future rents directly to the donee.
  • Directing the building society or flat owners' association to update their registry with the donee's name.
  • Applying online for e-Namjari mutation in the donee's name.

sections.h2: 9. Legal Irrevocability: Can a Registered Heba Be Cancelled Later?
sections.content:
A common dispute arises when a donor later falls out with a child and attempts to unilaterally cancel the gift deed:

Section 126 Transfer of Property Act & Islamic Personal Law: Once a Heba between close blood relations is registered and possession is delivered, it becomes completely and permanently irrevocable. The donor CANNOT unilaterally execute a cancellation deed (বাতিল দলিল) at the Sub-Registry. Any unilateral cancellation deed executed by a Sub-Registrar is illegal and void ab initio (39 DLR 353). A Heba can only be set aside by a formal civil court decree proving fraud, forgery, or coercion under Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act 1877.

sections.h2: 10. Post-Registration Protocol: e-Namjari Mutation & Online Khajna Update
sections.content:
Registration at the Sub-Registry transfers legal title, but it does NOT automatically update government land revenue records. To seal the transfer:

  1. Access the Ministry of Land mutation portal mutation.land.gov.bd within 28 days of deed issuance.
  2. Submit an application attaching the registered Heba deed, donor's Khatian, and both parties' NID/passports.
  3. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) conducts digital scrutiny, issues a formal Mutation Khatian in the donee's name, and issues a DCR receipt for BDT 1,150.
  4. Pay digital Land Development Tax at ldtax.gov.bd to generate government tax dakhilas in the child's name.

sections.h2: 11. Real-Life Case Study: New York Father Gifting a Banani Apartment to His Daughter
sections.content:
Background: Mr. Shawkat Hossain, an expatriate architect residing in Manhattan, New York, wanted to gift a luxury 2,400 sq. ft. residential apartment in Banani, Dhaka (market value BDT 4.2 Crore) to his newly-married daughter living in Toronto, Canada.

Execution Strategy:

  1. If executed as a sale deed, registration taxes would have exceeded BDT 45 Lakh ($38,000 USD).
  2. Our chamber structured the transaction as a simple Heba between Father and Daughter under the 33 blood relations rule.
  3. Mr. Shawkat executed a Special Power of Attorney at the New York Consulate, while his daughter executed a representative power in Toronto.
  4. Both deeds were authenticated at MOFA Segunbagicha and adjudicated at the Dhaka DC office.
  5. Our team attended the Tejgaon Sub-Registry, completed the registered Heba deed for under BDT 5,000 in official fees, and secured the digital e-Namjari Khatian within 21 days. Total savings: over $35,000 USD in avoided transfer taxes.

faqs.question: Can I gift a flat in Dhaka to my daughter living with me in the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can execute a Special Power of Attorney at the Bangladesh High Commission in London to register the Heba deed in Dhaka, transferring full title to your daughter with fixed BDT 100 stamp duty.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay capital gains tax on a Heba gift in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: No. Gifting property between eligible close blood relations is completely exempt from capital gains tax and advance source tax under Section 125 of the Income Tax Act 2023.

faqs.question: Can I give a Heba to my cousin, brother-in-law, or daughter-in-law under the BDT 100 rule?
faqs.answer: No. Cousins, in-laws, and step-relatives fall outside the designated 33 blood relationships. Gifting to them is treated as a general gift, attracting standard ad-valorem stamp duty (1.5%) and local registration taxes.

faqs.question: Can a father take back property gifted to his son after the Heba deed is registered?
faqs.answer: No. Under Muslim personal law and the Registration Act 1908, a registered gift to a direct lineal descendant becomes completely irrevocable upon registration and delivery of possession.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Heba and a Will (Wasiyat) in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: A Heba takes effect immediately during the lifetime of the donor and can cover 100% of assets. A Will takes effect only after death and cannot exceed 1/3rd of the estate without other legal heirs' consent.

faqs.question: Can a Hindu citizen execute a Heba deed in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: No. Heba is a concept exclusive to Muslim personal law. A Hindu citizen transfers property without consideration through a registered Gift Deed (দানপত্র দলিল) under the Transfer of Property Act 1882.

faqs.question: How long does the entire Heba deed registration and mutation take from abroad?
faqs.answer: Embassy execution abroad takes 3 to 5 days, MOFA and DC office stamping in Dhaka takes 2 to 3 weeks, Sub-Registry registration takes 1 day, and e-Namjari mutation takes approximately 28 working days.

faqs.question: Can minor children receive a Heba deed in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. A minor child can lawfully receive property via Heba; acceptance (Qubul) is formally executed on their behalf by their legal guardian (father, paternal grandfather, or court-appointed guardian).
